description:
File: crate-jmap-chat-server/src/backend.rs:278-282

  /// Returns true if this account supports the given JMAP object type.
  /// Called by the server consumer (e.g. the session capability builder) —
  /// NOT called internally by the handler library. Backends that support all
  /// types unconditionally can return `true` always.
  fn supports_type<O: JmapObject>(&self) -> bool;

The doc-comment explicitly says 'this account supports the given JMAP
object type' — but the signature has NO account_id argument. The
'this account' is implicit / unknown.

This is a real problem for production backends doing per-account
capability discovery. RFC 8620 §1.6.2 is unambiguous: capabilities
are per-Account, not per-server. A multi-tenant backend offering:

- Free tier: Chat, Message, Space, ChatContact (subset)
- Pro tier: + CustomEmoji, PresenceStatus
- Enterprise tier: + SpaceInvite, SpaceBan

literally CANNOT express the answer through this method, because
the answer depends on the account being queried and that account
id is not in scope.

This is also sync and stateless. Compare to ChatBackend::limits
(crate-jmap-chat-server/src/backend.rs:333) which DID get the
plumbing right: `fn limits(&self, _caller: &Self::CallerCtx,
_account_id: &jmap_types::Id) -> ChatLimits` — args plumbed even
in the default impl, so production backends can vary by-account
without an API break.

Three contract issues with the current shape:

1. The method's NAME ('supports_type') and DOC ('this account
   supports') promise per-account semantics. The signature
   silently delivers per-server semantics. A consumer reading
   the doc will write production code that compiles, runs, and
   silently returns wrong capabilities.

2. Once a single downstream backend depends on the
   no-account-id shape, adding account_id (or caller) is a
   breaking change. The current shape is locked in.

3. The doc says 'Backends that support all types unconditionally
   can return true always.' This describes the trivial case but
   doesn't admit the non-trivial case exists. A reader assumes
   the trivial case is the intended case.

Recommended fix (before publishing): match the limits() shape —
`fn supports_type<O: JmapObject>(&self, caller: &Self::CallerCtx,
account_id: &jmap_types::Id) -> bool` with the default impl
ignoring both args.

Sibling finding: JMAP-x2gd.43 calls out limits() sync-ness. This
finding is about the missing-args shape on supports_type, which
is a STRICTLY MORE SEVERE form of the same defect: limits has the
args (production can override per-account), supports_type does
not (production cannot).
title: API contract: ChatBackend::supports_type lacks account_id, blocks per-account capability discovery
